turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first: who decided that, and on what basis?
I spoke with the vice principal before you came in.

So the office knows before I do, again. What did you tell the vice principal, and is anything about this on Owen's record right now? If it is, it comes off today, or I'm in the principal's office tonight and the board after that.
She's backing me completely. Policy is policy, and it isn't up to you.

"Policy is policy." Then you broke it: your own procedure says the parent is contacted before any mark goes in, and the software alone doesn't establish anything. If the vice principal backs that, I'll have it in writing, so show me.
So frankly, this meeting is a courtesy.
A courtesy. You asked for this meeting, Hale, and you're running it like the decision was made before Owen was ever heard. Withdraw the zero, or I walk upstairs to the principal when we're done.
